title: Blindcap: Duel
hero: The mushroom knows. The pin tells you.
subhead: A 25-minute deduction game for two, built around a physical secret: buried tunnels make each probe rest low or stop high.
description:
Twelve mushrooms share a species-neutral silhouette above a cracked field, while visible bite marks still show which player owns each one. Each player knows the six species they plant and nothing about the other six. Three marked probes buy three public bits that remain on the field until harvest. Three crowns turn guesses into points. No cards, dice, app or moderator—the printed geometry resolves every probe.

By Alice.

use_case.label: On the table
use_case.body: Blindcap is for two people who like deduction but do not want one player to be the moderator. You hide a known mix of four mushroom species in plain sight. Your rival reads them one physical bit at a time, then commits crowns before the harvest turns every secret shank upward.

story_blocks.body: Each keyed mushroom can hide two parallel routes. Slide a probe through a marked tile channel: an open route lets it rest at 3 mm proud; solid shank stops it high at about 28 mm (27.63 mm digital reference). The pin stays in the tile until harvest, so the board holds every answer while decisions remain. No player announces a result, and no app keeps the state.

You receive exactly three probes. One reading cuts the four possible species to two. Reading both marked channels identifies a mushroom, but spending two probes in one place leaves the rest of the field dark. Every pin carries your mark, so useful questions—especially ones tied to your crowns—also resolve close games.

Crowns score connected groves after harvest. Two may be placed during the five main rounds; the third closes the game. A solo claim scores the grove size squared. If your rival contests it, both players score only its size. Inkcap and hollow groves score double.

Five turns force all three probes and both early crowns onto the board. You choose their order, but you cannot pass and gather perfect information. The round starter alternates, and both players seed the centre simultaneously, removing the old last-seat advantage without adding a compensating coin flip.

The four species share one silhouette above the loam while owner bites remain visible. A D-flat keys every shank so the one-dot and two-dot channels meet only their intended parallel route. The two trays screen six shanks from the opposite seat. Those relationships are the game, so the downloadable project carries editable STEP sources, per-part STL files, fit evidence and the coupon together.

The rules engine completes every simulated game and the current 400-game routing run is seat-balanced at 50.75% versus 49.25%, with 8.5% shared wins. The digital fit matrix clears every intended tunnel and blocks every absent route, including cross-talk. That is not human-play or physical-fit evidence. The private draft remains under review until printed coupons make both probe heights unmistakable and blind players complete the game unaided.
